title: Evidence for Chapter 33: Hicks's IS-LL (1937), the Oxford meeting of 1936, the American recession of 1937-38, Hansen (1939) and Pigou (1943), and the Bank of Japan in 1999-2001
source: Econometrica vol. 5 (1937): the report of the Oxford meeting of the Econometric Society (September 1936), the list of those who attended, and Hicks, 'Mr. Keynes and the "Classics"' (April 1937); Keynes, The General Theory (1936); the Federal Reserve Bulletin (August 1936, January and February 1937, March and May 1938); Banking and Monetary Statistics 1914-1941 (1943); Historical Statistics of the United States (1975), series Y 339-341; Velde (2009); Romer (NBER Working Paper 3829, 1991); Roosevelt's press conference of 2 April 1937 and message to Congress of 14 April 1938 (The American Presidency Project); Eggertsson and Pugsley (2006); the Bank of Japan's statements of 12 February 1999, 21 September 1999 and 19 March 2001; Hansen (American Economic Review, March 1939); Pigou (Economic Journal, December 1943); Modigliani's Nobel biography (1985) and the Econometric Society's page of his article of 1944; the U.S. Treasury's page on Henry Morgenthau Jr.; the authority records of the Library of Congress and the Bibliothèque nationale de France; the terms of the sites of the Federal Reserve Board, the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago and the Bank of Japan
series: Evidence rows: id, place, year, values (';' separated, in the order of the quotation), unit, source key, page or column, the source text verbatim, note
license: Quotations for criticism, scholarship and teaching, each with its source; no full original is redistributed. Econometrica vol. 5 (the report of the Oxford meeting, the list of those who attended, and Hicks's article): 'Copyright 1937 by the Econometric Society' (row hk_copyright); Hicks (1904-1989) is in copyright, so the chapter quotes short phrases only and paraphrases the rest; the snapshot keeps the sentences needed to check those phrases and the equations read on page images. Keynes (1883-1946): The General Theory (London: Macmillan, 1936) is in the public domain in the United Kingdom but may still be in copyright in the United States, so the chapter quotes it a sentence or less at a time. The Federal Reserve Bulletin, Banking and Monetary Statistics 1914-1941 (1943), Historical Statistics of the United States (1975), the pages of the U.S. Treasury and Roosevelt's press conference and message are works of the United States government and in the public domain. The Federal Reserve Board's site: 'Unless otherwise indicated, information on Board's website is in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission. Please cite to the Board as the source of the information.' (row fed_terms). The American Presidency Project: 'Online by Gerhard Peters and John T. Woolley, The American Presidency Project' (rows ap37_credit, ap38_credit). Velde (2009), Economic Perspectives of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago: the paper prints no reprint notice; the site's legal notice reads 'Copyright © 2026. All rights reserved.' (row vd_copyright) and 'Users may not reproduce, modify, publish, transmit, participate in the transfer or sale of, create derivative works from or in any way exploit any of the content, in whole or in part, of any copyrighted, trademarked or proprietary information owned by Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, except as expressly authorized by the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.' (row vd_terms): short phrases only. NBER Working Paper 3829 (Romer 1991) prints no copyright line; short phrases only. Eggertsson and Pugsley (2006): the abstract page reads 'Copyright © 2006 Bank of Japan All Rights Reserved.' (row ep_copyright) and the paper 'DO NOT REPRINT OR REPRODUCE WITHOUT PERMISSION.' (row ep_reprint); the Bank of Japan's terms do not cover the site of its Institute for Monetary and Economic Studies (row bj_imes): short phrases only. The Bank of Japan's statements: 'The information included in the site may be copied or reproduced with the exceptions below. When copying or reproducing, the source, the Bank of Japan, should be explicitly credited.' (row bj_terms). Hansen (1887-1975; American Economic Review, March 1939) and Pigou (1877-1959; Economic Journal, December 1943): the OCR texts of the issues print no copyright line; both are in copyright, so the chapter quotes short phrases only. Modigliani's biography on NobelPrize.org: 'Copyright © The Nobel Foundation 1985' (row nb_copyright): short phrases only; the Econometric Society's page gives only the title, issue and pages. The Library of Congress name authorities (id.loc.gov) are public data; the authority records of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (data.bnf.fr) are metadata reused under the Licence Ouverte (Open License).
citation: See the 'source' field; each row names its source key in the 'sources' object.
notes: Every quotation is checked word for word against the cached source text by data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py, and every value is read from its quotation by checks/check_ch33.py; rows with an empty quotation are values or words read on a page image (sources hicks1937img, hansen1939img, census_y33), named as such in their notes, which give a transcription between « and ». The figures of Banking and Monetary Statistics (Tables 105, 107, 122 and 128) were read on page images and are kept in the snapshots bms_member_reserves_1935_1939, bms_reserve_requirements_1917_1941 and bms_rates_1936_1940; the rows bms_* here quote the titles and headnotes from the text layer of the same scan. The OCR texts keep their misreadings as printed and the notes name them: in Econometrica, 'JS' for IS (hk_is, hk_monetary), 'J' for I (hk_directly), 'C(z)' for C(i) (hk_invest), '2', 'pz', 'Py' and '7' for x, px, py and i in Meade's list of variables (ox_dependent), 'zbid.' for ibid. (ox_refs) and the misread names of the list of those who attended (ox_attend), and 'Venture' and 'Setting' around Hicks's 'paraphrase the proof' (hk_paraphrase quotes only the phrase); in the Federal Reserve Bulletin, '331,' for 33⅓ (fb_331), 'diminsh' as printed (fa_deposits), ''and' and 'approxiimately' (fm_apr16), and a running head inside a sentence (fm_14bn); in Romer's working paper, the mixed brackets and 'Cordon' (rom92_hansen); in Hansen, '+' and '|' (hn_regimented); in Pigou, a running head inside a sentence (pg_vanish) and stray quotation marks (pg_unduly). Indirect testimony: Friedman and Schwartz (1963) through Romer (rows rom92_fs678, rom92_severe, rom92_steps: p. 678 and pp. 543-545) and through Velde (row vd_fs544: p. 544); Hansen (1938), Smithies and Gordon through Romer (rom92_hansen); Eccles's phrase 'pushing on a string' through Velde, who cites Meltzer (2003, p. 478) (vd_string); Currie, Calomiris and Wheelock, and Telser through Velde (vd_currie, vd_cause); Cole and Ohanian (1999, 2001, 2004) through Velde (vd_cole_timing, vd_cole2001, vd_steadystate); the Wall Street Journal of the day after the press conference of 2 April 1937 through Eggertsson and Pugsley (ep_wsj); Roosevelt's remark of 2 April 1937 through Eggertsson and Pugsley (ep_fdr) and in the transcript of the press conference (ap37_concerned). Modigliani's article of 1944 was not obtained (JSTOR answered with a bot check; archive.org has only the index of the volume); it is known here from his Nobel biography and from the Econometric Society's page. The Treasury's announcement of its gold policy is dated 21 December 1936 by the Bulletin of January 1937 (fj_dec21) and 22 December 1936 by the Treasury's press statement printed in the Bulletin of March 1938 (fr_dec22); the Bulletin of February 1937 dates the start of the programme 24 December 1936 (fb_dec24). Velde dates the peak of industrial production in May 1937 (vd_peakmay) and also measures the fall 'From its peak in July 1937' (vd_julypeak). The Bulletin of May 1938 puts excess reserves in August 1937 at $700,000,000 (fm_700m); Table 105 gives a monthly average of $750 million.
